newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Gov to call legislature back after Nov. polls.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Gov to call legislature back after Nov. polls.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki plans to call the legislature back into session after the Nov 5 elections for a special session on welfare, a spokeswoman for the governor said on Thursday.
She explained the govenor was waiting until after the polls because the legislators otherwise might be distracted by running their own campaigns.

"It's to ensure that everyone can come back to Albany and concentrate solely on this issue, and not be concentrating on their own campaigns." The spokeswoman had no information immediately available about what other issues the legislature might consider.

The special session is required to grapple with the changes imposed by the sweeping new federal welfare legislation, which shifts to a system of block grants for states and imposes new curbs. Pataki, who has set up a task force to study the issue, has estimated the extra costs will be in the hundreds of millions of dollars.

N.Y. comptroller H. Carl McCall has said that part of the new welfare program, the Temporary Assistance to Needy Families program, could produce a $250 million to $300 million surplus in its first year.
This new program replaces the Aid to Families with Dependent Children plan, which was the main federal cash welfare program.
